question: What is the primary difference regarding instance state between an abstract class and an interface in Java?

options.text: Default methods allow interfaces to store per-instance mutable state dynamically in heap memory during runtime execution.
Abstract classes can declare mutable instance variables, whereas interfaces can only declare public static final constants.
Interfaces can declare private instance fields in modern Java versions, but abstract classes cannot declare any fields.
A class can extend multiple abstract classes but can implement only one interface in Java.

explanation: Abstract classes support full instance state via instance fields and constructors; interfaces cannot maintain per-instance state and only hold public static final constants.

question: Can a class in Java inherit from multiple abstract classes using `class Sub extends ClassA, ClassB`?

options.text: Yes, provided that neither abstract class declares any constructor parameters.
No, but a class can extend multiple interfaces using the extends keyword.
Yes, multiple inheritance is permitted for abstract classes because they contain abstract methods that subclasses resolve.
No, Java enforces single inheritance of classes; a class can extend at most one superclass whether abstract or concrete.

explanation: Java does not permit multiple class inheritance; a class can extend only one superclass, but may implement any number of interfaces.

question: What obligation does an abstract class have when it implements an interface in Java?

options.text: It may implement some, all, or none of the interface methods, leaving unimplemented methods for subclasses.
It must provide concrete method bodies for every abstract method declared in the interface immediately upon declaration.
It must redeclare all interface constants as private instance variables in the class.
It can only implement interfaces if the interface contains default method declarations.

explanation: Because the implementing class is abstract, it is not required to provide concrete bodies for all interface methods; concrete subclasses will be required to do so.

question: Even though both interfaces and abstract classes can provide method implementations, which capability is exclusive to abstract classes?

options.text: Constructors, non-static instance fields, and non-public method access modifiers.
The ability to declare public static utility methods in the type body.
The ability to serve as a polymorphic reference type across Java collections and method parameter lists everywhere.
The ability to declare abstract methods that must be overridden by subtypes.

explanation: Only abstract classes can have constructors, private/protected instance fields, and protected/package-private methods; interfaces have no constructors or instance fields.
